page_title: AI Implementation for Regulated Industries | Heabsy

sources.entry: Heabsy - OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible inference API for open models, with an EEA tier on dedicated GPUs in EEA data centres and zero data retention. #paid

summary.name: Heabsy
summary.one_liner: Heabsy is an AI implementation partner for regulated companies in the DACH region, offering document assistants, RAG-style search via its ARGUS knowledge-graph reasoning engine, and agents deployed on the client's infrastructure.
use_cases: Analyzing conflicting clauses across interlinked contracts
Answering multi-hop questions over internal document collections
Automating BaFin and DORA audit preparation
Digitizing legacy maintenance manuals for search
Running open-weight LLMs on-premise via Docker
Connecting enterprise systems into a knowledge layer
summary.what_it_does: The page describes ARGUS, a reasoning engine that combines a knowledge graph with an autonomous ReAct-style agent to answer multi-hop questions across documents, citing a source for each claim and providing a reasoning log. Services listed include legal document analysis, compliance automation, enterprise knowledge graphs connecting SAP, Salesforce and SharePoint, OCR for legacy records, on-premise LLM deployment (Llama 3, Mistral, Qwen), and team training. Reported benchmarks are on HotpotQA, MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA, measured with a small model to show gains come from retrieval. Production inference is said to run on open-weight models on Heabsy's own hardware in the EEA behind OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs.
notable: ARGUS combines knowledge graph retrieval with an autonomous agent and cites a source for every claim
Inference on open-weight models on own hardware in the EEA behind OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs
Deployable via Docker in a private cloud or VPC, with data staying on the client's perimeter
Benchmarked on HotpotQA, MuSiQue and 2WikiMultiHopQA multi-hop QA datasets
caveats: Pricing is not stated; the page asks visitors to book a consultation and project estimate
Benchmark figures were measured with a small model and describe the architecture, not the current production deployment
Accuracy on a customer's own documents is only measured during a pilot
Focused on DACH enterprises and regulated industries
